data.title: Top 8 Solana APIs of October 2026
data.description:
Solana APIs are applications, websites, or bots that interact with the Solana blockchain. APIs essentially act as a messenger between software, letting applications ask for data or carry out a process. They are useful and help apps, services, or platforms work together across various systems.

APIs on Solana can help to retrieve wallet information and check SOL balances, token holdings and fetch transaction data and retrieve transaction history, and other details. Users can also access NFT data, ownership information, and digital asset details. Here are the top 8 Solana APIs for the month:

1. QuickNode

QuickNode provides a low-latency infrastructure and is built to scale dApps on the Solana blockchain. Developers can read blockchain data, submit transactions, interact with smart contracts, and build apps that need scalable blockchain connectivity.

It also aggregates traditional node infrastructure with advanced data products and transaction tools. Quicknode is great for developers who are building multi-chain dApps, NFT apps, DeFi platforms, and other enterprise blockchain solutions.

2. Helius

Helius offers a range of high-performance tools designed for speed and low latency, and gives users a chance to build Web3 applications and monitor transactions. It has a very user-friendly interface and simplifies complex blockchain interactions for its users.

The API has enhanced Solana RPC APIs and the Digital Asset Standard (DAS) API for NFT and token data. There is an option for real-time transaction and account monitoring along with webhooks for blockchain event notifications.

3. Alchemy 

Alchemy offers both access to real-time data and Solana infrastructure from the same provider, along with JSON-RPC and WebSocket connections. It also has Yellowstone gRPC for streaming live blockchain data and FAS and Photon APIs for tokens, NFTs, and compressed assets.

Solana Mainnet and Devnet are also supported, along with 99.99% reliability for its RPC and streaming API, multi-region infrastructure, and automatic failover to keep the connection running. Alchemy is used for wallets, DeFi apps, trading bots, custom indexers, and analytics platforms that need reliable RPC access as well as live Solana data.

4. Chainstack 

Chainstack is a node provider designed for teams looking for reliable blockchain access without having to run or build their own infrastructure. Both shared and dedicated nodes along with geo-distributed infrastructure for lower-latency access. More than 70 blockchains are supported on Chainstack, and a great option for team building applications across multiple networks.

There is a free tier for development and testing, while the paid plans scale based on factors such as throughput and node type rather than credits per API call. There is a 99.99% uptime and unlimited nodes for larger production workloads with stricter performance requirements.

5. ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW is different from other APIs as it focuses on crypto swaps more than on Solana data or node access. Wallets, dApps, exchanges, and payment platforms add in-app swaps without having to build their own exchange logic, liquidity routing, or transaction processing.

It supports 1,500 assets across 110+ blockchains with over 2.25 million exchange pairs and liquidity sourced from both centralized and decentralized exchanges. There are reports of 99.99% availability and a 350-millisecond response time.

6. CoinAPI 

CoinAPI focuses on crypto market data rather than direct access to the Solana network. Users can get data from 300 exchanges through a single API, giving developers access to real-time and historical SOL trades, quotes, order books, and OHLCV data.

There is also pay-as-you-go access with $25 in free monthly credits, and fixed plans start at $79 per month for Startup, followed by $249 for Streamer and $599 for Pro. Paid plans also include a 99.9% uptime SLA, while latency guarantees are available through custom Enterprise plans.

7. Moralis

Moralis supports EVM chains and Solana, and the API focuses on making blockchain data accessible through simple REST endpoints. It also focuses on token data, pricing, and NFT metadata, and gives a higher-level abstraction than raw RPC.

Users also get instant access to cross-chain blockchain data and allows users to pull normalized DeFi positions across major protocols via single API calls.

8. CoinStats

CoinStats gives developers actionable information instead of making them work with raw transaction data on Solana. It covers data from more than 120 blockchains and 10,000+ DeFi protocols that can be useful for wallets, tax tools, portfolio trackers, and dashboards that need to work across multiple networks.

There is also a credit-based pricing model, with requests using 30-50 credits depending on the endpoint. The free plan includes 50,000 monthly credits and up to 5 requests per second, while the paid plans start at $49 per month for 1 million credits.

Final word

Solana has a growing developer ecosystem which creates demand for reliable APIs that simplify blockchain connectivity and data access. APIs help developers build apps that can read data from and interact with and send transactions to the Solana blockchain.

User discretion is advised, and users should do their own research before investing.

data.title: Analyzing BNB’s rebound opportunities hours after $6.3B hack, altcoin sell-offs
data.description:
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, reported a security breach incident with an estimated total impact of $6.3 billion. At the time of writing, roughly $3 billion of the affected assets had been frozen on-chain.

The incident caused panic in the markets and led to a Bitcoin [BTC] sell-off. In the 12 hours before press time, BTC’s price fell by 5.2% from $81.7K to $77.4K. Crypto liquidations measured $1.50 billion in the last 24 hours, with $1.28 billion in longs liquidated.

Binance Coin [BNB], the exchange token, fell by a commensurate 5.2% over the same time period. Co-founder and former CEO of Binance, Changpeng Zhao, assured users that funds were safe, pointing to Chief Customer Service Officer Yi He’s statement on X and the rapid response from Tether and Circle to freeze the affected assets.

Popular crypto analyst and trader Ali Martinez suggested that a buying opportunity could be around the corner. The $73K-level for BTC, Ethereum [ETH] at $2,000, and XRP at $1 would be his buy-the-dip targets.

Where would BNB offer such a similar opportunity?

On the 1-day chart, the swing structure flipped bearishly with a daily session close below $703.6. This level was the latest swing low in BNB’s uptrend from under $600 in August.

The price bounce from $680 to $718 at the time of writing brought the altcoin back into the Value Area, highlighted within the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool.

Plotted from the previous swing low, this tool marked the Value Area High (VAH) at $711 and VAL at $770, and the Point of Control at $750.

Traders’ call to action – Buy!

The latest bounce has brought BNB back within the short-term range from mid-September. However, the daily structure saw a bearish change of character. Hence, despite the bounce, swing traders need to be cautious.

BNB seemed to be presenting a risky buying opportunity. A deviation below the local range on the back of an unforseen news event like Binance’s hack, followed by a swift recovery, may be a possibility.

Whether this bullish scenario comes true depends on capital inflows that will be dictated by Bitcoin and the wider market’s sentiment.

Final Summary

  • Binance’s security incident has severely shaken market sentiment and led to a crypto market liquidation cascade.
  • BNB saw a sizeable retracement below its Value Area and will need to reclaim $700 with strong demand to keep the bullish bias alive.

data.title: QNT crypto’s price now down 50.5% from September’s high — Should you buy now?
data.description:
Quant [QNT] has shed 50.5% of its value from the $373-high it made on 27th September. The most recent losses saw QNT crypto’s price fall below the psychological $200-support.

News of the Binance hack to the tune of an estimated $6.3 billion, the largest in history, has also driven markets into a selling frenzy. In fact, Bitcoin [BTC] slipped below the $80k round-number level too, spurring altcoin losses.

In this environment of steady selling and a month-long retracement, Quant might be offering a high-risk short-term buying opportunity. Swing investors might want to wait a bit longer for a momentum shift confirmation before looking to re-enter.

Sizeable September rally keeps current structure firmly bullish

The swing structure on the daily chart was bearish, captured by the Fibonacci retracement levels (orange). At the time of writing, the 61.8% retracement level at $178.8 was being respected as support.

Even so, the internal structure was bearish, as evidenced by the price dip below $223.5 earlier this month to form a new local low at $173.56.

In the coming days, a daily session close below $173.5 would be a sign that QNT’s price was heading towards the 78.6% retracement level at $126.

Traders should remember that sentiment remains fragile following the Binance hack news.

QNT’s price bounce expected due to H4 shift

The 4-hour chart seemed to be more encouraging though. The bullish structure shift made earlier this week, when the price broke above the $212.87-swing level, was still intact. The subsequent retracement back towards $180 might be ending.

The technical indicators did not yet show a reversal. The OBV was balanced between buying and selling pressure, and the RSI moved below neutral 50.

Based on the price action, buying QNT at these prices could be feasible. The bullish target would be $223.5, while invalidation lay below $173.56.

As the daily chart showed, a drop below $173.5 could see a QNT price slide all the way down to $126.

Final Summary

  • The Clearing House partnership and cascading long squeezes fueled QNT’s bull trend.
  • A price drop below $173.5 would signal QNT price weakness, but for now, the narrative could regain strength if the wider market begins to recover.

data.title: 10% to 56%: USDC’s remarkable rise in euro-paired stablecoin trading
data.description:
Since December 2023, USD Coin [USDC] has increased its market share of euro-paired stablecoin trade from 10% to 56% as of October.

While at the end of 2024, euro-paired stablecoin trade volume reached levels near $10 billion per month before declining in subsequent months.

As a result of MiCA restrictions on Tether [USDT], the number of transactions using USDC increased. This gave USDC an advantage as it pushed more trading activity toward USDC.

Julia Kovalchuk, Head of B2B Product at Paybis, a MiCA-licensed crypto and fiat infrastructure provider, told AMBCrypto in an exclusive interview, 

After MiCA, USDC grew from about 21% to 75% of stablecoin volume among our payment-firm clients in a year. The US leans toward USDC too, while USDT still dominates trading and emerging markets. Winners are regional and split by use case – USDC is the default choice for enterprise payment companies, traditional-finance on-ramps, and regulated custody in both the EU and the US.

Specifically, since Tether had been denied access to euro markets, euro-paired USDC order books now have 40% more depth than those of USDT/EUR order books.

Therefore, larger euro-paired stablecoin trades were able to be executed without causing as much price movement.

This gives USDC an advantage for traders converting euros into dollar-backed stablecoins. Nevertheless, the global supply of USDT is 2.5 times larger than that of USDC.

The 56% level of euro-paired trading of USDC, however, indicates how regulation may be able to move trading activity and liquid assets from one stablecoin to another.

MiCA rules give USDC an edge over USDT in Europe

The shift in market leadership demonstrates a much broader trend of changes occurring in the European regulatory environment.

MiCA established a July 2026 deadline for all stablecoin issuers to obtain EU authorization and demonstrate they comply with reserve and supervision requirements.

Still, Tether’s USDT remains unauthorized. However, Circle received authorization via a French electronic-money license. In response to the regulations, Coinbase began restricting USDT trading for its European customers.

AMBCrypto asked Kovalchuk what compliance means in a world governed by MiCA-style regulations. She responded,

In Europe, liquidity is easy to find. A license takes years and costly legal work, so many smaller firms plug into licensed infrastructure like ours. The US GENIUS Act, Hong Kong’s Stablecoins Ordinance, and the UAE’s payment token rules point the same way.

Coinbase is also converting any outstanding amounts of non-compliant USDT for its European customers around the 30th of October. Meanwhile, the European Banking Authority designated USDC a significant e-money token in mid-October, bringing it under direct supervision.

Therefore, these regulations are also establishing a framework for how exchanges can service European users.

Ethereum stablecoin addresses surpass 300M

The Ethereum [ETH] stablecoin ecosystem has continued expanding, reaching over 300 million holder addresses. However, the fact that there are over 300 million holder addresses does not automatically mean that there are as many unique and active users.

Approximately three-quarters of these holders reside on layer two networks. This highlights the role that Layer 2 networks have played in increasing access to stablecoins.

When asked if stablecoin gains on Layer 2s translate to real adoption or just balances that flow back to L1, Kovalchuk noted,

Some of both. Part of L2 volume is still trading balances moving back to exchanges. The growth to watch is repeat use: payouts, merchant settlement, and payroll. Once the same businesses settle on L2 every week, that L2 has become a payment rail.

Lower fees associated with layer two networks make it cheaper for individuals to transfer funds using stablecoins. Increased levels of network usage may indicate that individuals are more likely to utilize the same stablecoin multiple times.

But if a few regulated issuers hold most of the market, who carries the risk when one fails? According to Julia,

Holders carry the risk, which is why MiCA’s reserve and redemption rules matter. Europe has moved from one dominant stablecoin to another, so concentration is worth watching. Businesses should ask their platform how many stablecoins it supports and how quickly it can switch if one is restricted.

Together, these trends could shape future competition between USDC and USDT. Ultimately, lasting leadership will depend on regulatory access, deep liquidity, and sustained user activity.

Final Summary

data.title: Strategy’s STRC nears $100 – Will Michael Saylor resume Bitcoin buys?
data.description:
STRC price has climbed to $99.92 and is close to its $100 peg, raising hopes that it could allow Strategy to renew its Bitcoin [BTC] buys. 

According to VanEck’s head of digital asset research, Matthew Sigel, a historical pattern suggests the world’s largest Bitcoin treasury firm could soon kick off BTC buys again.    

STRC back to $99.9. Last time it regained par (Jan 6th), the ATM was restarted the next business day to buy Bitcoin. Given relatively low volumes, MSTR buyback (~$950M remaining) may be having an outsized impact at these levels.

STRC, one of Strategy’s preferred stocks, crashed to nearly $70 in June amid rising concerns that the firm could be forced to liquidate BTC to fund its active dividend obligations. Bitcoin also dropped below $60K at that time, further raising market fears. 

It has since recovered to $99.9 in the past few months, amid a broader market rebound, STRC buybacks, and a standby cash reserve to cover dividend payouts during a market lull. 

Will Strategy boost Bitcoin value?

STRC sales were instrumental in BTC buys in the first half of 2026. That changed in H2 2026, as shown by the chart. More of the MSTR ATM sales helped fund STRC buybacks (purple) and cash reserves. 

The firm has now bought back $2.05B of STRC. It bought back another $200 million in STRC and zero BTC last week. Now that its daily dividends for STRC and other preferred stocks have been officially adopted, it’s unclear how much demand they will attract.  

While STRC is the most liquid US preferred stock, VanEck’s Sigel flagged it as overvalued, but added, 

I’m very underweight DATs: you overpay management for unpredictable leverage. But if this reaches par, it’s probably a positive for BTC and MSTR, on the margin.

That said, Strategy currently holds 848.5K BTC and has acquired over 216K BTC since last August. In fact, it was responsible for 71% of Bitcoin treasuries’ demand over the same period, buying over 216K BTC. 

But as mentioned earlier, the bulk of the purchases happened in late 2025 and H1 2026. As Strategy BTC bids cooled in 2026, other treasury firms offloaded their holdings. Since mid-October, BTC’s overall demand turned negative, and ETFs became net sellers. 

With no Strategy bids to absorb the pressure, Coinbase analysts warned that the low demand could drag BTC below $80K if the trend persists later in the year. 

Final Summary

  • VanEck projected that Strategy could renew its BTC buys as STRC inches closer to $100.
  • Strategy drove 71% of treasury demand for BTC since late 2025, but the bids cooled in H2 2026.

data.title: HOOD stock falls 8.5% as Robinhood’s crypto revenue weakness draws attention
data.description:
The Robinhood Markets HOOD stock fell 8.55% to $83.76 in early trading on October 30, extending its October decline. Its price opened well below the price it closed at on Thursday as cryptocurrency markets faced fresh uncertainty surrounding Binance’s security incident.

The selling comes days after Robinhood reported a 55% annual drop in quarterly crypto revenue. Its latest results offer a useful measure of its exposure as investors assess the fallout across crypto markets.

Crypto revenue falls despite record company sales

The Robinhood third-quarter results that was published on October 27, showed that crypto revenue was $120 million. This amount made up about 8.4% of the total revenue.

The total revenue reached a record $1.424 billion, up 12% year over year. Options brought in $399 million, while event contracts brought in $173 million.

Those businesses helped to make up for the crypto decline. But net income fell 14% to $476 million, and earnings per share dropped 16% to $0.51.

Binance adds uncertainty to the backdrop

In an October 30 update, Binance estimated that the impact of its security incident was about $6.3 billion. But it said that about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.

The exchange temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals during security checks, and it said it would cover losses with its emergency reserve.

For Robinhood, the question is how customers respond to the event.

As could be seen on the chart, HOOD was already declining before the security reports.

HOOD loses ground below $90

At the time of this writing, HOOD was trading at around $83.76.

Its price opened at $85.21, compared with $91.59, where it closed the previous day, and it dropped to the $82.34 price level before it recovered a bit.

A look at its trend over the past week showed that it has declined from its September highs above $120. The repeated declines it has seen in October had already brought its price below $100 ahead of Friday’s opening drop.

It remains to be seen if HOOD can hold above the $82.34 price level it dropped to during the session. Around $80 provides another nearby reference area. If it recovers toward the $89–$92 price area, it would return its price to the range it occupied in the last sessions.

Final Summary

HOOD dropped by 8.55% to trade at $83.76 on October 30, extending an earlier decline.

Robinhood’s quarterly crypto revenue fell by 55%, while other businesses supported record total revenue.

data.title: Kraken outage affects Spot and derivatives trading – Here’s what happened
data.description:
Kraken, one of the world’s major cryptocurrency exchanges, experienced a temporary technical disruption on the 30th of October 2026, affecting both spot and derivatives trading.

According to Kraken’s status dashboard, the issue began at 02:42 UTC and prevented some users from connecting to the platform and successfully submitting orders.

What happened to Kraken?

The disruption affected Kraken’s website and mobile application, along with its REST, WebSocket, and FIX APIs. For those unaware, these interfaces allow retail traders, institutional clients, and automated trading systems to access market data, connect to the exchange, and execute trades.

In simple words, this disruption might have caused difficulties for users trying to log in to their accounts, access trading services, place buy or sell orders, or execute trades through automated systems.

However, Kraken confirmed that the incident was resolved at 03:42 UTC, approximately one hour after it was first reported. But what is more important here is that this disruption did not indicate a security breach or loss of customer funds. In fact, it was more of a connectivity and order-processing issue.

Kraken’s demand remains uninterrupted

This follows the exchange witnessing growing demand for round-the-clock trading through its xStocks platform, which offers tokenized versions of traditional stocks.

This is because now more than 50% of xStocks trading volume now takes place outside conventional stock market hours. In other words, investors are increasingly looking for the flexibility to trade beyond standard exchange timings.

Additionally, Kraken has also expanded its xStocks offerings to over 1,000 listings since last week, broadening access to tokenized equities for millions of users worldwide.

Notably, AMBCrypto’s recent report suggested that Kraken was in a spotlight back on the 24th of October. On that day, Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi had apologized for emails sent to Monero [XMR] buyers requesting personal information, including employment details, proof of income, bank statements, and intended use of withdrawn funds.

Crypto hacks are on the rise

Like Kraken, Binance too announced plans to resume withdrawals within 48 hours following a temporary suspension for security checks after a reported $6.3 billion hack.

Still, according to DeFiLlama data, the cryptocurrency industry has witnessed a sharp rise in security incidents in 2026, with 322 confirmed hacks recorded so far, already more than double the total reported in 2025.

In fact, threats also remained active recently, with 12 confirmed hacks reported in just the past seven days, highlighting the persistent vulnerability of the crypto ecosystem to cyberattacks.

Final Summary

  • The disruption affected Kraken’s website and mobile application, along with its REST, WebSocket, and FIX APIs.
  • Kraken confirmed that the incident was resolved at 03:42 UTC, approximately one hour after it was first reported.

data.title: XRP Ledger to tighten permissioned token rules to attract institutional players
data.description:
XRP Ledger plans to tighten rules on who can hold permissioned, regulated tokens such as stablecoins or tokenized stocks. In an upgrade named fixCleanup3_5_0, which bundles four proposals, XRP Ledger intends to remove loopholes that currently allow unapproved users to hold regulated assets without issuer approval. 

For some tokenized stocks, issuers want to screen whoever is buying their tokens for compliance checks, including anti-money laundering (AML) and manipulation risks. As such, a permissioned environment allows issuers to run identity checks.

Until now, XRP Ledger has had ways to bypass this, which can derail onboarding of institutional players leveraging tokenized stocks and other regulated assets on the network. This is part of the chain’s push to advance and position itself for the tokenization boom. 

What’s next for the XRP Ledger proposal

The proposals were pushed out earlier this week. At the time of writing, the upgrade was yet to be merged into the main software, the next stage for validator consensus and potential adoption into the mainnet network. 

To advance to the next phase, the upgrade must get 80% validator support, or about 29 out of 35 trusted validators, for two weeks. 

Since the AI-flagged decade-old $90B risk to the network in September, the team has been actively scanning for flaws and vulnerabilities as part of continued hardening of the protocol. The advanced AI models have also elevated security risks to blockchains and digital systems. 

According to the XRP Ledger Foundation, the recent upgrade proposal is part of routine hardening of the protocol and not related to any security incident. 

So, will the proposal improve XRP Ledger ratings in the tokenization race?

XRP Ledger’s tokenized stocks traction

According to the RWA dashboard, XRP Ledger is the 10th largest network with $642.5M in tokenized assets. This is slightly below Base, which holds $650M of tokenized assets and ranks 9th. 

Interestingly, among the top 10, Base and XRP Ledger saw the largest growth in tokenized assets in the last 30 days. XRP Ledger’s value grew by 28% while Base’s traction increased by 69%. 

Overall, XRP Ledger is seeing traction on the tokenization front and wants to improve the underlying tech to advance the segment while ensuring compliance guardrails for institutional players. 

Final Summary

  • XRP Ledger is eyeing an upgrade to restrict unauthorized users from holding regulated tokenized assets and stablecoins. 
  • Network is ranked 10th in tokenized assets value with $642.5M, following a growth of 28% in October.

data.title: Curve DAO loses $0.30 support – Why CRV faces further downside risks
data.description:
Curve DAO [CRV] recorded a sharp decline of 17.08% in the last 24 hours at press time, continuing to extend its recent decline as selling pressure intensified. Meanwhile, Spot trading volume surged 182% to $94.49 million, highlighting increased market participation during the sell-off. 

The rapid volume increase along with the declining prices together pointed to aggressive selling as opposed to renewed buying interest. Additionally, the derivatives analytics also revealed another concerning development as market participants reduced their exposure.

Notably, the decline also coincided with a broader crypto market crash, as the Fear and Greed Index fell to 38, reflecting growing investor fear.

Derivatives surge, but traders abandon CRV positions

The trading volume on CRV derivatives rose 126.53% to $221.82 million as of writing, reflecting increased volatility in the Futures markets. 

Despite increased trading, Open Interest (OI), however, declined 19.23% to $110.77 million,  suggesting a considerable decrease in active positions. These contrasting figures implied investors closed their positions instead of committing fresh capital to the market.

Generally, declining OI during a sudden price decline usually points toward position unwinding and potential liquidations. Such developments often tend to go hand-in-hand with periods of market uncertainty as leveraged traders exit the market. 

Exchange reserves shrink despite CRV’s steep decline

At the time of writing, the token’s Exchange Reserves fell 15.58% to $120.9 million in 24 hours, highlighting a significant reduction in exchange-held token value.

However, it is also worth noting that the reserve decline also reflected CRV’s falling price, which limits conclusions about actual token withdrawals. On the other hand, the Spot Netflows, meanwhile, remained predominantly negative, with October 30 recording roughly $218,990 in net outflows.

Typically, continued negative netflows imply reduced immediate selling availability as traders transfer tokens away from exchanges.

Despite these withdrawals, however, CRV’s price continued declining, suggesting that existing selling pressure had overwhelmed potential accumulation. This divergence raised questions on whether the reduced exchange supply could eventually be of help in stabilizing CRV price. 

Can CRV defend its next critical support?

CRV’s technical structure  on the daily chart confirmed a breakdown below $0.30, a region that previously supported several price recoveries. The bears pushed prices toward $0.2739 following the breakdown, bringing the next major support at $0.2372 into the spotlight.

Furthermore, the RSI indicator dropped to 30.24 as of writing, nearing the oversold territory and reflecting intense bearish pressure. Besides, the indicator’s position below its moving average further highlighted the fading buying strength.

The MACD indicator validated the bearish outlook, with its line falling to below the signal line, and the negative histogram expanding to -0.0030.

Ultimately, CRV remained vulnerable after losing the $0.30 support zone, while the declining Open Interest and bearish indicators strengthened the downside risks. 

Even though the exchange outflows offered potential relief, the bears still retained control, and failure to recover the $0.30 support could expose CRV to further losses toward $0.2372.

Final Summary

  • CRV’s 17% crash coincided with falling Open Interest and persistent market fear.
  • CRV could extend losses toward $0.2372 unless buyers reclaim the $0.30 level.

data.title: Binance to resume withdrawals within 48 hours after $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance plans to allow withdrawals in 48 hours after a precautionary pause to conduct security checks following the recent hack. In the exchange’s latest service update, Yi He, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of the exchange, said, 

Deposits remain unaffected and continue to operate as normal. Our team is currently working on enhancements to the withdrawal service and related address controls. We expect to begin resuming withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.

The hack began at around 20:20 UTC on Thursday, 29th October, targeting Binance’s primary Ethereum hot wallet.

About 2 hours later (22:30 UTC), Binance acknowledged the exploit and issued the first statement of a potential attack. It suspended all deposits and withdrawals and opened investigations. 

Binance hack update: Nearly $3B stolen funds frozen

In a follow-up, the world’s largest crypto exchange said estimated stolen funds were about $6.3B. This was at 02:25 AM UTC on Friday, 30th October 2026. That’s about 3 hours after the initial preliminary investigation announcement. 

The $6.3B figure makes the Binance hack the largest ever in crypto history. The attacker drained Binance hot wallets across 10 chains. 

On Ethereum, the attacker siphoned $3.74B worth of crypto assets. On the Bitcoin network, the attacker stole 18,270.2 BTC worth $1.47B. On TRON, the hacker moved $612.7M USDT and 46.4M TRX (total $627M). Solana, Arbitrum, and Avalanche recorded $96M, $32M and $24M drains, respectively. 

In fact, the Ethereum and Bitcoin drains dominated 83% of the $6.3B heist.

Industry partners, including Tether, Circle, Ripple, Paxos, Arbitrum, World Liberty Financials, and Binance itself, have frozen about $2.8B already. That’s nearly half of the heist, most stablecoins with freezing features. 

However, the attacker can still move BTC and ETH assets, worth about $3.27B, according to on-chain and security analyst Dickson Wu.  

According to Web3 security investigator Zachary Wolk (popularly known as ZachXBT) and Chainalysis, North Korea’s TraderTraitor was behind the hack, citing commingling of Binance’s stolen funds with Bitget’s $388M exploit address.  

For its part, Binance traced the exploit to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. This allowed TraderTraitor to gain access to the exchange’s internal infrastructure and sign off on transfers.

The exchange also maintained that there were no wallet private key leaks and pledged to cover all losses. 

Impact of the Binance hack

The hack soured market sentiment to ‘fear’ levels last seen in August. It dropped BTC’s value by 7% to $76.5K, before an attempted rebound. 

However, analyst Benson Sun downplayed the hack’s impact on Bitcoin, noting that it will take years to liquidate. In doing so, he drew a parallel to the Coldcard and Bitfinex hacks. 

So, the stolen BTC looks like bad news on the surface, but it’s actually a disguised form of locked-up supply.

Final Summary

  • Binance estimates total stolen funds to be $6.3B, with half of the stash now frozen.
  • Stolen $1.5B BTC won’t be sold immediately, but ETH could face more pressure.
